items.title: Teenage Sleep
items.text: Many teenagers struggle to wake up early, and parents often blame laziness. However, scientists point to biology instead. During adolescence, the body begins to release the sleep hormone melatonin later at night, so young people feel awake long after adults feel tired. As a result, a student who goes to bed at midnight may get only six hours of sleep before a seven o'clock class. Some schools have therefore moved their start times back by an hour. In these schools, attendance improved and students reported feeling less stressed. Clearly, the problem was never simply a lack of discipline; it was a mismatch between the school schedule and the teenage body clock.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Parents should punish teenagers who keep refusing to get up early.
Teenagers' sleep trouble has a biological cause that schools can address.
Melatonin pills help students fall asleep sooner and study harder.
Attendance rises whenever a school makes its lessons an hour shorter.
qs.why: 마지막 문장이 요지를 정리해요: 문제는 규율이 아니라 학교 시간표와 생체 시계의 불일치예요.

qs.q: What does 'these schools' refer to?
o: Schools that ask students to sleep before midnight
Schools that lowered the number of morning classes
Schools that ended classes an hour earlier than before
Schools that moved their start times later
qs.why: 앞 문장의 'moved their start times back by an hour'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the writer use 'However' in the second sentence?
o: To introduce a view that contradicts the parents' opinion
To give a further example of how lazy teenagers can be
To show that scientists agree with what parents believe
To describe what happened after schools changed schedules
qs.why: However는 앞의 '게으름 탓'과 반대되는 과학자들의 설명을 이끌어요.

qs.q: How much sleep might a student get who goes to bed at midnight and has a seven o'clock class?
o: About eight hours
About nine hours
About six hours
About seven hours
qs.why: 글에서 'only six hours of sleep'라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?
o: Teenagers who sleep late are less intelligent than adults.
Schools should remove all rules about arrival times.
A fixed early timetable can work against teenagers' natural rhythm.
Adults need more melatonin than young people do.
qs.why: 'mismatch between the school schedule and the teenage body clock'에서 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: Bike Lanes
items.text: When the city council proposed a protected bike lane on Harbor Street, many shop owners objected. They feared that removing parking spaces would drive customers away. Nevertheless, the council went ahead with a one-year trial. Surprisingly, sales along the street did not fall; in fact, they rose by almost ten percent. Researchers explained that people on bicycles stop more often than drivers do, and they tend to visit the same shops repeatedly. Moreover, the street became quieter and safer, which encouraged more people to walk. The shop owners who had complained now ask the council to extend the lane to the next block. Their change of mind shows how evidence can beat first impressions.

qs.q: What was the shop owners' original worry?
o: Fewer parking spaces might mean fewer customers.
Cyclists might damage the goods displayed outside.
The trial might last longer than a single year.
Quieter streets might make the shops less popular.
qs.why: 'removing parking spaces would drive customers away'라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the word 'Nevertheless' tell us about the council's decision?
o: It gave up the plan completely because of the shop owners' objections.
It waited until the owners changed their minds.
It asked the owners to design a new trial.
It went on with the plan despite the objections.
qs.why: Nevertheless는 반대에도 불구하고 계획을 진행했다는 대조를 나타내요.

qs.q: According to the researchers, why did sales rise?
o: Drivers parked closer to the doors and spent much more time inside the shops.
Cyclists stop often and come back to the same shops.
Prices fell after the bike lane was completed.
Tourists visited the street to photograph the lane.
qs.why: 연구자들은 자전거 이용자가 자주 멈추고 같은 가게를 반복해서 방문한다고 설명했어요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To draw a general lesson from the story
To warn readers against building more bike lanes
To introduce a new group of people in the story
To describe the exact results of the research
qs.why: 마지막 문장은 사례에서 일반적인 교훈(증거가 첫인상을 이긴다)을 끌어내요.

items.title: The Bee Problem
items.text: Bees are small, but their work feeds much of the world. About one third of the food we eat depends on pollination, the process in which pollen moves from one flower to another so that fruit can form. Almonds, apples and blueberries, for example, all rely heavily on bees. Unfortunately, bee populations have been shrinking in many regions. Scientists link the decline to several causes, including disease, the loss of wildflower meadows and certain farm chemicals. Because these causes overlap, no single solution is enough. Some farmers have begun leaving strips of wildflowers beside their fields, and gardeners are planting flowers that bloom in different seasons so that bees can find food all year.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How almonds and apples are grown on large farms
Which flowers produce the sweetest honey for bees
Why bees matter and what is putting them at risk
Why farmers should stop using any chemicals at all
qs.why: 벌의 중요성과 감소 원인, 대응을 다루는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which of the following is given as an example of food that depends on bees?
o: Potatoes and carrots
Blueberries
Rice
Bananas

qs.q: Why does the writer say 'no single solution is enough'?
o: Farmers refuse to cooperate with the scientists.
Each region has its own kind of bee.
Wildflowers cannot grow near farm fields.
The causes of the decline are connected to one another.

qs.q: What is the purpose of planting flowers that bloom in different seasons?
o: To make gardens look attractive in winter
To stop diseases from spreading between bees
To replace the fruit trees on nearby farms
To give bees a steady supply of food
qs.why: 'so that bees can find food all year'가 목적이에요.

qs.q: Which word best replaces 'link' in 'Scientists link the decline to several causes'?
o: separate
connect
forget
measure
qs.why: link A to B는 'A를 B와 연결 짓다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Paper Library
items.text: Some people predicted that e-books would make printed books disappear. Instead, the two formats have settled into a kind of partnership. Readers who travel a lot prefer e-books because a whole shelf fits inside a single device. By contrast, students often choose paper when they need to study, since flipping pages helps them remember where an idea appeared. Libraries have adapted as well: many now lend both versions and even offer quiet rooms for people who want to read without screens. In short, the new technology has not replaced the old one but has given readers a wider choice. What matters most is not the format but whether the reader enjoys the book.

qs.q: What did some people predict about e-books?
o: They would be cheaper than library membership.
They would be read only by students and travelers.
They would cause printed books to vanish.
They would improve the way people remember ideas.

qs.q: The phrase 'By contrast' introduces
o: a different preference from the one just mentioned
a result of what the previous sentence said
an example of the previous sentence's idea
a repeated explanation of the same reader

qs.q: Why do students often choose paper books for study?
o: Paper books are always cheaper than devices.
Turning pages helps them recall where information was.
Libraries do not allow e-books in study rooms.
Printed books are written with fewer difficult words than e-books.
qs.why: 'flipping pages helps them remember where an idea appeared'

qs.q: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?
o: E-books have finally defeated printed books in public libraries across the world.
Printed books are better than e-books for every kind of reader.
Libraries have stopped lending books in order to save money.
E-books and printed books exist side by side, each suiting different readers.

items.title: Why Dough Rises
items.text: Bread dough rises because of tiny living things called yeast. When yeast is mixed with flour and water, it feeds on the sugars in the flour. This feeding produces carbon dioxide, a gas that forms thousands of small bubbles inside the dough. The dough is stretchy, so it expands around the bubbles instead of letting them escape. If the baker kneads the dough well, the structure becomes strong enough to hold the gas. Then, when the dough is put in a hot oven, the bubbles grow even bigger before the heat finally stops the yeast and fixes the shape of the loaf. That is why a good loaf is light and full of holes.

qs.q: What causes bubbles to form in the dough?
o: Yeast producing gas as it feeds on sugar
Water turning into steam before baking
Flour reacting with the salt in the recipe
The baker pressing air in with both hands

qs.q: What does 'them' refer to in 'instead of letting them escape'?
o: the sugars and flour
the bakers
the bubbles
the loaves

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens in the oven?
o: The yeast multiplies until the loaf is fully cooked.
The dough shrinks and the gas escapes quickly.
The bubbles expand until the heat stops the yeast.
The flour turns into sugar that feeds the bubbles.
qs.why: 열이 효모를 멈추게 하기 전까지 거품이 더 커져요.

qs.q: How is the passage organized?
o: It explains a process step by step.
It compares two different recipes for bread.
It tells a story about a baker's first day.
It argues that bread should be made at home.
qs.why: 효모가 거품을 만들고 오븐에서 모양이 고정되는 순서로 과정을 설명해요.

items.title: Coral in Trouble
items.text: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they shelter about a quarter of all sea creatures. Corals get their color and much of their food from tiny algae living inside them. When the water becomes too warm, the corals push the algae out, and they turn white. This is called bleaching. A bleached coral is not yet dead, but it is weak, and if the warm water lasts too long it will starve. Therefore, even a small rise in sea temperature can threaten an entire reef community. Scientists are now testing heat-tolerant corals in the hope that they can be planted where reefs have been damaged.

qs.q: Why do corals turn white?
o: They absorb too much light from the surface.
They are eaten by fish that live in the reef.
They cannot find enough algae in cool water.
They expel the algae that give them color and food.
qs.why: 물이 너무 따뜻해지면 산호가 조류를 내보내 하얗게 변해요.

qs.q: What does the word 'Therefore' show?
o: A contrast with the earlier description
A conclusion drawn from the previous statements
An example of a bleached reef
A change in the topic of the passage

qs.q: Which statement is true according to the passage?
o: A bleached coral can survive if the warm period ends soon.
Corals can get all their food without any algae.
Reefs cover about a quarter of the ocean floor and shelter most fish.
Heat-tolerant corals have already saved every reef.
qs.why: 'not yet dead'와 'if the warm water lasts too long it will starve'에서 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the scientists' tests?
o: Strongly doubtful
Completely certain
Hopeful but cautious
Entirely uninterested
qs.why: 'in the hope that they can be planted'는 기대하되 확정적이지는 않다는 어조예요.

items.title: The Audio Guide
items.text: At first, Mina thought the audio guide at the museum would be boring. She preferred to wander freely and read the labels beside each painting. But her little brother insisted on borrowing one, so she agreed to try it. To her surprise, the voice told stories that the labels never mentioned: where a painter lived, what he was afraid of, even what he ate for breakfast. Suddenly, the portraits did not look like old pictures anymore; they looked like people. By the end of the afternoon, Mina had asked to keep the headphones for another hour. She still enjoys reading labels, but now she knows that a good story can make an object come alive.

qs.q: How did Mina feel about the audio guide at first?
o: She was eager to use it.
She expected it to be dull.
She was afraid of the headphones.
She was angry with her brother.
qs.why: 'thought the audio guide ... would be boring'

qs.q: What does 'Suddenly' signal in the passage?
o: A warning about a danger in the museum
A reason why Mina wanted to leave early
A description of what the labels said
A change in how Mina saw the portraits
qs.why: Suddenly 이후에 그림을 보는 방식이 바뀌었어요.

qs.q: Why did Mina use the audio guide?
o: The museum required every visitor to borrow one.
The labels beside the paintings were missing.
She had read good reviews about the voice.
Her brother wanted one and she agreed to try.
qs.why: 'her little brother insisted ... so she agreed'

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
o: Labels are less accurate than recorded voices.
Stories can add meaning to things we simply look at.
Museums should stop printing information on walls.
Paintings are interesting only to young visitors who like stories.
qs.why: 이야기가 물건을 살아 있게 만든다는 의미예요.

items.title: Warm Floors
items.text: Traditional Korean houses were heated by ondol, a system that warms the floor instead of the air. Smoke and hot air from a fireplace in the kitchen traveled through channels under stone slabs, and the stones kept the heat for hours. As a result, people sat and slept on the floor, and the furniture was low and light. In summer, however, the same houses stayed cool because the main hall had a wooden floor that let breezes pass underneath. This combination of two floors shows how builders solved the problem of very different seasons. Today, modern apartments use hot-water pipes in place of smoke channels, but the idea of a warm floor remains the same.

qs.q: How did the ondol system heat a room?
o: Heated water ran through clay pipes built inside the walls of each room.
A stove in the middle of the room warmed the air.
Hot air from the kitchen fire warmed the stones under the floor.
Sunlight was stored in large wooden boards.
qs.why: 부엌의 열기가 바닥 아래 통로를 지나 돌을 데웠어요.

qs.q: Why was furniture in these houses low and light?
o: People used the floor for sitting and sleeping.
Stone was too expensive for large furniture.
Wooden floors could not support heavy objects.
The houses were too small for tall chairs.
qs.why: As a result 앞의 내용이 원인이에요.

qs.q: What does 'however' show in the fourth sentence?
o: A repetition of the winter heating method
A contrast between winter and summer arrangements
A reason why stones keep heat for hours
An example of modern apartment heating

qs.q: According to the passage, what has stayed the same in modern apartments?
o: The use of smoke channels
The low and light furniture
The wooden hall for summer
The idea of a warm floor

items.title: Phones and Memory
items.text: Many people take photos of everything they see, believing that the pictures will help them remember. Psychologists, however, have found the opposite. In one experiment, visitors to a museum were asked to photograph some objects and only look at others. Later, they remembered fewer details about the objects they had photographed. The researchers suggest that when we rely on the camera, our brain treats the task of remembering as already done. This does not mean that photography is harmful. Rather, it suggests that we should sometimes put the phone down and pay full attention. A photo can preserve how a place looked, but only attention can preserve how it felt.

qs.q: What did the experiment find?
o: People remembered less about objects they had photographed.
People remembered more about objects they had photographed.
People forgot every object they had looked at.
People could not tell which objects were in the museum.
qs.why: 사진 찍은 물건에 대한 세부 기억이 더 적었어요.

qs.q: What does 'Rather' do in the sentence 'Rather, it suggests that we should sometimes put the phone down'?
o: It adds a further reason against photos.
It repeats the result of the experiment.
It corrects a possible misunderstanding.
It introduces an unrelated topic.
qs.why: '사진이 해롭다는 뜻은 아니다. 오히려...'로 오해를 바로잡아요.

qs.q: What does 'the task' in 'the task of remembering' most likely mean?
o: selling pictures to visitors
drawing a map of the museum
keeping information in the mind
writing a report about the objects

qs.q: Which is the best conclusion of the passage?
o: Attention, not only pictures, is needed to remember an experience.
Taking photographs is the best way to remember.
Museums should forbid every kind of camera on their premises for good.
Memory improves when people look at fewer objects.

items.title: Giving Time
items.text: Last winter, a group of students in our school began visiting a nursing home every Saturday. At first, they felt shy and were not sure what to say. The residents, meanwhile, seemed equally nervous. That changed when one student brought a deck of cards. Within minutes, the room was full of laughter as old and young argued over the rules. Over the following weeks, the students learned that a visit does not need a special plan; simply listening to a life story can be a gift. They also discovered that they received as much as they gave. One of them said later, 'I went to help, but they taught me patience.'

qs.q: Why was the first visit uncomfortable?
o: The residents did not want any visitors.
The students had no time for a conversation.
The nursing home had strict rules for guests.
Both groups felt unsure about how to begin.

qs.q: What changed the mood of the room?
o: A story about the school
A deck of cards
A song from the residents
A gift from the principal

qs.q: What does the student's last comment suggest?
o: Volunteering can teach the helper something too.
Nursing homes need more professional helpers.
Older people are usually impatient with students.
Students prefer cards to any other activity.

qs.q: What is the purpose of 'meanwhile' in the third sentence?
o: To show that the students had changed their plan after the first week
To show that the visits ended in the winter
To show that the residents' feelings were happening at the same time
To show that the residents were happier than students

items.title: Training Slowly
items.text: Anyone who decides to run a marathon quickly learns that enthusiasm alone is not enough. Beginners often start by running too far, too fast, and they end up with sore knees within two weeks. A better approach is to increase the weekly distance by only about ten percent. Although this seems painfully slow, it gives muscles and bones time to adapt. Experienced coaches also insist on rest days, because the body becomes stronger during rest rather than during the run itself. Finally, runners should practice drinking and eating during long runs, so that nothing surprises them on race day. Patience, in other words, is as important as speed.

qs.q: Why do beginners often hurt their knees?
o: They refuse to take any rest days between their runs at all.
They run too far and too fast at the start.
They wear shoes that are too heavy.
They forget to drink during long runs.
qs.why: 'start by running too far, too fast'

qs.q: The word 'Although' in 'Although this seems painfully slow' introduces
o: a reason for the ten percent rule
a list of the coach's exercises
an example of an experienced runner
an idea that is opposite to the result that follows
qs.why: 느려 보이지만 근육이 적응할 시간을 준다는 양보 관계예요.

qs.q: According to coaches, when does the body become stronger?
o: While running uphill
While drinking water
While stretching before a race
While resting

qs.q: Which statement best expresses the writer's message?
o: Marathon runners should avoid every long run.
Gradual preparation matters as much as fast running.
Ten percent is the fastest speed for beginners.
Only experienced coaches can train a marathon team.
qs.why: 마지막 문장: Patience is as important as speed.

qs.q: What is the function of 'Finally' in the passage?
o: It shows that the race has finally ended for the runner.
It introduces a surprising failure.

items.title: After the Bottle
items.text: Every plastic bottle has a long future ahead of it. Some are collected, cleaned and melted down to be made into new products such as jackets or carpets. This process, called recycling, saves oil and reduces waste. However, not every bottle gets this chance. If a bottle is dirty or mixed with other materials, the factory may reject it. For this reason, experts recommend rinsing bottles and removing their caps before putting them in the recycling bin. Even then, plastic can be recycled only a few times before its quality drops. That is why many scientists argue that the best solution is to use less plastic in the first place, rather than to depend on recycling alone.

qs.q: What is the main argument of the passage?
o: Recycling helps, but using less plastic is better.
Plastic bottles can be recycled forever without change.
Factories should reject every dirty bottle they receive.
Jackets made of bottles are better than cotton jackets.

qs.q: What does 'this chance' refer to?
o: being rinsed carefully with clean water
being turned into new products
being collected in a factory
being sold in a store

qs.q: Why do experts recommend rinsing bottles?
o: Clean bottles weigh much less when they are transported.
Caps are made of a more valuable material.
Rinsed bottles can be reused by families.
Dirty bottles may be rejected by the factory.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned?
o: The price of recycled products
The use of recycled bottles in clothing
The limit on how often plastic can be recycled

items.title: Uniform Debate
items.text: Whether students should wear school uniforms has been argued for decades. Supporters say that uniforms reduce pressure about clothing, since nobody can show off expensive brands. They also claim that uniforms create a feeling of belonging. Opponents, on the other hand, believe that clothes are a form of self-expression, and that forcing everyone to dress alike limits individuality. Some studies have tried to settle the question, but their results disagree, perhaps because schools differ so much. A fair-minded reader might therefore conclude that the effect of uniforms depends on how they are introduced and whether students have a voice in the decision. Both sides, after all, want the same thing: a school where everyone feels comfortable.

qs.q: Which is an argument made by supporters of uniforms?
o: They allow students to express their personalities.
They are cheaper than every other kind of clothing.
They lessen the pressure to wear fashionable clothes.
They improve the grades of students in all schools.

qs.q: What does 'on the other hand' introduce?
o: An example of a school with uniforms
The conclusion of the studies
The opposing side of the debate
A reason supporters agree with opponents

qs.q: Why do the studies disagree, according to the writer?
o: Schools are very different from one another.
Students never answer questions honestly.
Supporters have paid for different studies.
Uniforms look different in each country.

qs.q: What is the writer's position?
o: In favor of uniforms
Against uniforms
Completely unconcerned about the topic being discussed
Neutral, presenting both views fairly
qs.why: 양쪽을 공정하게 소개하고 마지막에 공통 목표를 말해요.

items.title: The Night Train
items.text: Travelers who choose the night train often say that the journey itself becomes part of the holiday. You board in the evening, eat dinner in a small dining car, and fall asleep to the steady rhythm of the wheels. By morning, the view outside has changed completely, from city lights to open fields. Compared with flying, the train takes longer and is rarely cheaper. Nevertheless, it saves the cost of a hotel night, and it avoids the long ride to and from an airport. Many passengers also appreciate that the trip produces far less carbon dioxide per person. For these reasons, night trains are returning to routes where they had almost disappeared.

qs.q: What is one advantage of the night train mentioned in the passage?
o: It is always cheaper than an airplane ticket.
It saves the cost of a night in a hotel.
It arrives earlier than any other transport.
It allows passengers to choose the scenery.
qs.why: 'saves the cost of a hotel night'

qs.q: What does 'Nevertheless' contrast with?
o: The train taking longer and not being cheaper
The passengers falling asleep to the wheels
The change in the view outside by morning
The dinner served in the small dining car
qs.why: 단점을 먼저 말하고 Nevertheless 이후 장점을 말해요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'it avoids the long ride to and from an airport'?
o: the holiday itself
the hotel
the night train
the airport

qs.q: Why are night trains returning to some routes?

items.title: Tides
items.text: Anyone who has spent a day at the seaside has noticed that the water level rises and falls twice a day. These movements, called tides, are caused mainly by the moon. The moon's gravity pulls on the ocean, creating a bulge of water on the side of the Earth facing it. A second bulge forms on the opposite side, because the Earth is also pulled away from the water there. As the planet turns, each coastline passes through both bulges, and so it experiences two high tides every day. The sun also has an effect, though a smaller one. When the sun and moon line up, their combined pull produces especially high tides.

qs.q: What mainly causes the tides?
o: The wind blowing across the sea
The heat of the sun on the water
The rotation of fish near the coast
The pull of the moon's gravity

qs.q: Why do coastlines have two high tides a day?
o: The moon passes the Earth twice in an hour.
The sun and moon pull in opposite directions.
The sea is lifted by the wind twice a day.
The Earth turns through two bulges of water.

qs.q: What does 'one' in 'a smaller one' refer to?
o: a tide
an effect
a coastline
a bulge
qs.why: 'The sun also has an effect, though a smaller one'

qs.q: What can be inferred about days when the sun and moon line up?
o: There are no tides on the coasts at all.
The water level changes only once.
The sea level at high tide is greater than usual.

qs.why: 두 천체의 인력이 합쳐져 특히 높은 조수가 생겨요.

items.title: Small Shops Online
items.text: For many small shop owners, the internet at first looked like a threat. Large websites could offer lower prices and deliver within a day. Yet some shops have found that going online can actually help them. A flower shop, for instance, began taking orders through a simple website and found that customers in neighboring towns could now buy from it. In addition, the shop used social media to show its newest arrangements, which attracted young customers who had never walked through its door. The owners say that the personal touch remains their strength: they still write each card by hand. The internet did not replace their business; it widened the street outside it.

qs.q: How did the flower shop benefit from the internet?
o: It reached customers in other towns.
It lowered its prices below the large websites.
It stopped writing cards for its customers.
It closed its physical shop for good.

qs.q: What does the phrase 'In addition' do?
o: It contrasts the flower shop with large websites.
It adds another benefit to the previous one.
It gives a reason for the lower prices.
It shows the result of the customers' complaints.
qs.why: 첫 번째 이점에 두 번째 이점을 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What does the final sentence mean?
o: The shop moved to a wider street in the center of town.

qs.why: 'widened the street'은 비유로, 고객과 접점이 넓어졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which statement is true?
o: The owners value their handwritten cards.
Large websites could not deliver within a day.

qs.why: 'they still write each card by hand'

items.title: A Roof Garden
items.text: On top of an old office building, a group of neighbors has created a small garden. At first, the owner doubted that anything would grow so high above the street, where the wind is strong and the soil is thin. The gardeners solved this problem by choosing hardy herbs and by building low walls that block the wind. Now they harvest mint, basil and tomatoes, which they share with local restaurants. The garden also helps the building itself: the plants keep the roof cooler in summer, so the air conditioners use less electricity. Even the birds and butterflies seem to approve, as they have started to visit regularly. What was once an empty roof has turned into a small community project.

items.title: Learning by Living
items.text: Language teachers often say that the fastest way to learn a language is to live where it is spoken. This is partly true. When you must order food, ask for directions and make friends in the new language, you hear it constantly and you cannot avoid using it. On the other hand, living abroad does not guarantee success. Some people spend years in another country but speak only with others from home, so their progress is slow. The key, therefore, is not the place itself but the amount of real communication. Students who cannot travel can still create a similar effect by watching films, joining online conversation groups and writing to pen friends.

items.title: Practice Drills
items.text: Every autumn, schools in earthquake-prone areas hold safety drills. Students first learn to drop to the ground, take cover under a desk and hold on until the shaking stops. Next, they walk calmly to an open area while a teacher counts heads. Some students find the exercise silly because they have never felt a strong earthquake. Yet experts insist that practice matters. In a real emergency, people tend to freeze or panic, and a habit learned in advance can take over when thinking becomes difficult. In that sense, a drill is similar to learning to ride a bicycle: you do not reason about each movement, you simply act. The few minutes it takes could save a life.

items.title: The Busker's Hat
items.text: Every Friday evening, an elderly man plays the violin outside the subway station. Most commuters hurry past him with their eyes on the ground. One rainy night, however, a girl stopped, took off her earphones and stood still until the song ended. When she dropped a coin into his hat, he lifted his head and smiled, and she smiled back. She did not tell him that it was her first day in a new city, nor that she had been feeling lonely. The next Friday she returned and listened again. Neither of them spoke, but the small ritual made her feel that she belonged somewhere. Sometimes a stranger's music is all that is needed.

items.title: Failing Forward
items.text: Our robotics club spent two months building a robot that could pick up small balls and drop them into a basket. On the day of the competition, it worked perfectly in the practice round. Then, in the first real match, its arm froze and the robot stood motionless while the other teams scored point after point. We were crushed. Afterward, however, our teacher asked us to examine what had gone wrong. It turned out that a single loose wire had caused the problem. We realized that we had never tested the robot after moving it by bus. Next year, we will repeat the test under travel conditions, and we will carry spare parts. Failure, it seems, can be the most useful teacher.

items.title: Noise and Focus
items.text: Many students claim that they study better with music playing, but research suggests the truth is more complicated. Quiet background sounds, such as soft rain or gentle instrumental pieces, can help some people relax. In contrast, songs with lyrics compete with the words you are reading, because the brain has only limited space for language. The effect also depends on the task. A simple, repetitive job like copying notes may go well with music, whereas solving a hard math problem usually does not. Therefore, the best advice is to match the sound to the work. If you notice that you have read the same line three times without understanding it, it may be time to press pause.

items.title: Fertile Slopes
items.text: Around many volcanoes in the world, farmers have lived for centuries despite the obvious danger. The reason is simple: volcanic ash breaks down into rich soil full of minerals that plants need. Crops grown on these slopes, such as coffee, grapes and rice, often produce larger harvests than those on ordinary land. Of course, the risk is real, and eruptions can destroy fields within hours. Even so, many families choose to stay, relying on warning systems that monitor the mountain day and night. Their decision may seem strange to outsiders, but it follows a clear logic. When the possible gain is large and the danger can be watched, many people judge that the balance favors staying.

items.title: Time Zones
items.text: Before the nineteenth century, each town set its clocks by the sun, so noon in one city could be several minutes different from noon in the next. This caused few problems as long as people traveled slowly. When railways appeared, however, timetables became a nightmare, because a train could cross many local times in a single afternoon. To solve the problem, countries began dividing the world into zones in which everyone uses the same time. Today there are more than twenty zones, and some of them differ by only thirty or forty-five minutes. Although this system is far from perfect, it allows airlines, banks and families on different continents to arrange meetings without confusion.

items.title: Shorter Showers
items.text: A typical shower uses about sixty liters of water, which may not sound like much until you multiply it by every person in a city. One family in our neighborhood decided to measure its habits. They placed a small timer in the bathroom and discovered, to their surprise, that the average shower lasted twelve minutes. After they set a goal of seven minutes, their water bill dropped by a noticeable amount within a month. They also noticed an unexpected side effect: since the bathroom was less steamy, mirrors stayed clear and the mold on the ceiling stopped growing. Their experience shows that big savings often come from small changes, provided that we first find out what we are really doing.

items.title: Is It a Sport?
items.text: Competitive video gaming, or e-sports, now fills stadiums and offers prize money larger than many traditional tournaments. Fans argue that gamers need quick reactions, teamwork and hours of training, just like athletes. Critics reply that sitting at a screen cannot count as sport because there is little physical effort. The disagreement partly depends on what we mean by the word 'sport'. If it means a contest of physical strength, e-sports fail the test; if it means a contest of skill, they pass it. Whatever label we choose, one fact is clear: the players practice seriously, and their audiences are growing. Perhaps the more useful question is not what to call it, but how to keep players healthy.

items.title: Thin Air
items.text: Climbers who go above three thousand meters often feel dizzy, tired or short of breath. The cause is not that the air contains less oxygen, which is a common belief; the proportion of oxygen stays the same. Instead, the air pressure is lower, so each breath delivers fewer oxygen molecules to the lungs. To compensate, the body breathes faster and makes more red blood cells over several days. For this reason, experienced mountaineers climb in stages, spending a few nights at middle heights before going higher. Those who rush upward risk altitude sickness, which can be serious. As the mountaineers say, the mountain does not care how fit you are; it only cares whether you give your body time.

items.title: Pen or Keyboard
items.text: In a well-known study, students who took notes by hand were compared with students who typed. Both groups heard the same lecture. When tested a week later, the handwriters answered conceptual questions better. Researchers think the reason lies in how each group worked. Typists can record nearly every word, so they often copy without thinking. Handwriters cannot write as fast, which forces them to choose what is important and to put it in their own words. That mental effort strengthens learning. This does not mean that computers are useless in class; they are excellent for searching and organizing. It simply reminds us that the easiest method is not always the one that teaches us the most.

items.title: Ant Highways
items.text: When one ant finds food, it does not call the others. Instead, it walks back to the nest leaving a faint trail of chemicals. Other ants smell the trail and follow it, and each one that finds food adds more chemicals on the way home. In this way, a shorter route receives more visits in the same time, so its smell becomes stronger than that of a longer route. Soon almost all the ants use the best path, although no single ant has planned it. Engineers have borrowed this idea to design computer programs that find efficient routes for delivery trucks. It seems that even tiny creatures can teach us about solving large problems.

By the second day, however, we had learned to paddle at the same moment, and we passed the whole class. Last night we cooked rice over a fire, and it was slightly burnt, but nobody complained. The best part was floating in silence under the stars. I did not think I would enjoy being away from my phone, yet I hardly missed it. I will tell you more when I get home. Love, Jiho

Perhaps the most sensible step is to teach children early how advertisements work, so that they learn to ask: who made this, and why?

items.title: Long Flights
items.text: Every year, millions of birds travel thousands of kilometers between their summer and winter homes. How do they find their way? Scientists believe that birds use several tools at once. They watch the position of the sun by day and the pattern of stars by night. In addition, they sense the earth's magnetic field, which works like an invisible map even under cloudy skies. Young birds, making the trip for the first time, may simply follow adults, while the adults rely on memory of landmarks such as rivers and coastlines. When one tool fails, another can take over. Meanwhile, the physics teacher turned the panels into a classroom, because a screen in the hallway now shows how much electricity is being produced each hour. Members pay a small fee, return the items on time and care for them as if they were their own. Not everything about the system is easy, however. Volunteers must repair damaged tools, and popular items are often unavailable on weekends. Even so, the libraries are growing, perhaps because they offer something modern shopping rarely does: a chance to meet your neighbors.

items.title: The Missing Page
items.text: When the school magazine was printed, the editors discovered that page twelve was blank. Everyone blamed the printer at first, but Soyeon, the youngest editor, quietly checked the files. She found that the page had been saved under a different name, so the program had skipped it. Instead of pointing out who had made the mistake, she simply fixed it and reprinted the page that evening. The next morning, the head editor thanked her in front of the team. Soyeon only shrugged and said that errors are easier to repair when nobody is afraid of them. The remark surprised the older members, who realized that a calm attitude had saved more time than any argument could have.

qs.q: What caused the blank page?
o: The printer ran out of ink halfway through the printing.
The file had been saved under another name.
The editors forgot to write it.
The magazine was too long.

qs.q: How did Soyeon respond to the problem?
o: She argued with the printer.
She told the head editor who was at fault.
She solved it without blaming anyone.
She waited for the next issue.
qs.why: 'Instead of pointing out who had made the mistake'

qs.q: What does 'The remark' refer to?
o: her comment about errors and fear
the head editor's thanks
the printer's explanation
the magazine's title

qs.q: What is the main message?
o: Young members always make fewer mistakes.
A calm, blame-free attitude solves problems efficiently.
Printers are the main cause of errors.
Editors should work alone in the evening.

items.title: Seeds Underground
items.text: Deep inside a mountain in the far north, there is a vault that holds duplicates of seeds from crops around the world. Its purpose is not to grow anything today but to protect the future. If a disease or a disaster destroyed a variety of wheat in one country, scientists could ask for a sample from the vault and begin again. The storage rooms are kept cold, and the rock around them provides natural protection against heat and earthquakes. Because the seeds are only copies, each country continues to own its own samples. Critics sometimes say that the vault is an expensive precaution, but supporters answer that insurance always looks costly until the day it is needed.

qs.q: What is the vault's main purpose?
o: To grow food for the countries nearby during emergencies
To sell rare seeds to scientists
To study the cold climate of the north
To keep backup copies of the world's crop seeds

qs.q: Why are the seeds called 'copies'?
o: Each country keeps its original samples.
They are made of plastic that keeps well in the cold.
They grow only in cold rooms.
They were taken from the mountain.

qs.q: What does the comparison with insurance suggest?
o: The vault will earn a lot of money for its owners someday.
Scientists should buy seeds yearly.
A precaution may seem costly until a crisis occurs.
Crops are cheaper than insurance.
qs.why: 필요한 날이 오기 전까지는 비싸 보인다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What do the rock walls around the storage rooms provide?
o: Hidden storage away from thieves
Protection from heat and earthquakes
Water that keeps the seeds moist
Fuel for the cooling machines
qs.why: 바위가 열과 지진으로부터 자연스럽게 보호해 줘요.

items.title: Wind at Sea
items.text: Offshore wind farms are rising in many coastal waters, and the reasons are easy to understand. Winds over the sea are stronger and steadier than those on land, so each turbine produces more electricity. In addition, there are few buildings to block the view, which reduces complaints from residents. On the other hand, building at sea is expensive: the towers need strong foundations, and workers must travel by boat for repairs. Fishermen also worry that the structures will take up good fishing grounds. Engineers respond that the foundations can become homes for shellfish and small fish, and some wind farms already permit fishing between the towers. Whether the benefits outweigh the costs will depend on careful planning for each location.

qs.q: Why do offshore turbines produce more electricity?
o: The winds at sea are stronger and steadier.
The towers at sea are always taller.
Fishermen help to keep them running.
There is more sunshine over the water.
qs.why: 바다 위의 바람이 더 강하고 꾸준해요.

qs.q: What does 'On the other hand' introduce?
o: Another advantage of wind at sea
A result of the fishermen's complaint
An example of a coastal town
A disadvantage after the advantages

qs.q: What does 'the structures' refer to?
o: the boats used by workers for repairs at sea
the wind turbines and their foundations
the fishing grounds
the residents' houses

qs.q: What is the writer's conclusion?
o: The value of a wind farm depends on its location and planning.
Wind farms at sea should be abandoned because of their enormous cost.
Wind farms are always better on land.
Fishermen should decide every project.

items.title: Choosing a Club Trip
items.text:
Hana: Have you decided where the photography club should go this spring?
Minsu: Not yet. There are two options: the old fortress town or the harbor market.
Hana: The fortress is beautiful, but it is a two-hour bus ride away.
Minsu: True. On the other hand, the market is only twenty minutes from school, so we would have more time to take pictures.
Hana: That is a good point. However, the market will be crowded on a Saturday, and it might be hard to photograph without people in the frame.
Minsu: Then we could go on a weekday afternoon instead, since the stalls are open until six.
Hana: Our class ends at three, so that would work. And if the weather is bad, we can shoot under the roof.
Minsu: Great. Let's propose the market to the teacher tomorrow.

o: Planning the next school festival with the whole class

Scheduling a bus for a field trip

qs.q: Why does Hana hesitate about the fortress town?
o: It is closed on weekdays.
It takes two hours to get there.
It is too crowded on Saturdays.
It costs a lot to enter.

qs.q: Why does Minsu suggest going on a weekday?
o: To arrive before the market opens
To spend more time on the bus
To have the teacher join them
To avoid the weekend crowds at the market

qs.q: What does 'that' refer to in 'that would work'?

photographing without people
asking the teacher tomorrow

qs.q: What do the speakers finally agree to do?

Suggest the market to their teacher

Take a vote among all members

items.title: A Disagreement in a Group
items.text:
Jiwoo: I have finished my part of the presentation, but I think the order of the slides is confusing.
Daeun: Really? I thought it was fine. It starts with the problem and ends with the solution.
Jiwoo: Yes, but the example about plastic bags comes before we explain why plastic is a problem. People might wonder why we mention it.
Daeun: I see what you mean. Because the example needs the background, we should switch those two slides.
Jiwoo: Exactly. Also, the conclusion repeats the introduction almost word for word.
Daeun: Hmm, that is on purpose. I wanted the audience to feel that we had come full circle.
Jiwoo: That is a nice idea, but maybe we could add one new sentence about what the audience can do. Otherwise, it sounds like we learned nothing.
Daeun: Fair enough. Let me rewrite the last slide tonight.

qs.q: What is Jiwoo's first concern?
o: The presentation is too long for the time they have.
The slides contain spelling mistakes.
The sequence of the slides is hard to follow.
The plastic bag example is incorrect.

qs.q: Why should the two slides be switched?
o: The example needs the background to make sense.
The problem slide is too short to explain the background.
The audience dislikes examples.
The solution is already clear.

qs.q: Why did Daeun repeat the introduction in the conclusion?
o: She ran out of time to write a new one.
She wanted to create a feeling of coming full circle.
The teacher required it.
She forgot what the introduction said.

qs.q: What does Jiwoo mean by 'Otherwise, it sounds like we learned nothing'?
o: The audience will leave early.
The group will receive a bad grade.
The introduction must be deleted.
Without a new sentence, the ending adds nothing.
qs.why: 새 문장이 없으면 결론이 발전 없이 보여요.

qs.q: How does the conversation end?
o: Daeun agrees to revise the last slide.
Jiwoo takes over the whole presentation.
They decide not to change anything.
They ask the teacher to choose.

items.title: Which Laptop?
items.text:
Seoyeon: I can't decide between these two laptops. The first is cheaper, but it is quite heavy.
Salesperson: That is correct. It has a bigger screen, though, and a more powerful processor.
Seoyeon: I carry my computer to school every day, so weight matters to me. How long does the battery of the lighter one last?
Salesperson: About twelve hours. The heavier model lasts only six.
Seoyeon: Twelve hours would cover the whole school day. But the lighter model costs a hundred dollars more.
Salesperson: Yes. If you mainly write documents and watch videos, you won't notice a difference in speed. The extra money is really for the weight and the battery.
Seoyeon: In that case, it is worth it. I would rather pay more once than carry something heavy for three years.
Salesperson: Sensible choice.

The size of the screen
How easy the laptop is to carry
The brand of the processor

qs.why: 추가 비용은 무게와 배터리를 위한 것이에요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'it is worth it'?

the school day
the salesperson's advice
paying a hundred dollars more
qs.why: 백 달러를 더 내는 것이 가치 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which expresses Seoyeon's reasoning at the end?
o: She wants to spend as little as possible.
A single higher cost is better than years of discomfort.
She dislikes the salesperson.

items.title: Homework Debate
items.text:
Mr. Park: Today's topic is whether schools should assign less homework. Eunji, would you start?
Eunji: Yes. I believe homework should be reduced, because many students sleep only five or six hours. Fatigue makes it harder to learn.
Taemin: I disagree. Homework gives students a chance to practice what they learned, so it helps them remember.
Eunji: Practice is important, but quality matters more than quantity. Thirty carefully chosen questions are better than a hundred repetitive ones.
Taemin: I accept that point. Nevertheless, without any homework, some students would not review at all.
Mr. Park: So is there a middle path?
Eunji: Perhaps short assignments that are checked and discussed in class.
Taemin: Then I could agree, as long as the tasks are meaningful.
Mr. Park: Thank you both. You have shown that a disagreement can lead to a better idea.

qs.q: What reason does Eunji give for reducing homework?
o: Students do not get enough sleep.
Teachers do not read the answers.
Homework is too easy for students.
Students prefer working in class.

qs.q: What is Taemin's main argument?
o: Homework should be longer.
Quality is less important than quantity.
Homework helps students retain what they learned.
Teachers should not check homework.

qs.q: Why does Taemin say 'Nevertheless'?
o: He changes his mind completely after hearing Eunji's reply.
He accepts a point but still keeps his position.
He ends the discussion.
He introduces a new topic.
qs.why: Nevertheless는 양보 후 입장 유지를 나타내요.

qs.q: What compromise is proposed?
o: No homework on weekends or during school holidays
Longer assignments done in groups
Optional homework for every subject
Short assignments that are checked in class

qs.q: What is the purpose of Mr. Park's final remark?
o: To announce a test for the next week's class
To criticize both students
To change the topic
To point out the value of constructive disagreement
qs.why: 의견 충돌이 더 나은 아이디어로 이어진다고 정리해요.

items.title: Rescheduling the Festival
items.text:
Yuna: Did you hear that the school festival has been postponed?
Jun: Yes, because the weather forecast predicts heavy rain on Friday. The principal doesn't want students to perform on a wet stage.
Yuna: That makes sense, but my band has practiced for weeks, and we planned everything for that day.
Jun: Don't worry. The new date is the following Wednesday, so you'll have extra time to rehearse.
Yuna: That's one way to see it. Still, the drummer has a dentist appointment on Wednesday afternoon.
Jun: Then ask the committee to place your band in the morning program.
Yuna: Good idea. Since the schedule isn't printed yet, they might agree.
Jun: I'll go with you to the committee room after lunch if you like.
Yuna: Thanks. That would give me courage.

o: The stage was not ready.

The principal was away.
Too few students signed up.

qs.q: What does Yuna mean by 'That's one way to see it'?
o: She completely agrees with Jun.
She does not understand Jun.

She wants to cancel the festival.

The band cannot rehearse.

The schedule has not been printed yet.
The band is the most famous.
Wednesday is a holiday.

qs.q: How does Yuna feel at the end of the conversation?
o: Angry with the committee

items.title: Planning a Weekend Trip
items.text:
Ben: I would like to visit the island this weekend, but I'm worried about the ferry.
Mira: Why? Is it expensive?
Ben: No, the ticket is cheap. The problem is the timetable. The last ferry back leaves at five, so we would have only four hours on the island.
Mira: Four hours is short, but we don't need to see everything. We could rent bicycles and ride around the coast.
Ben: That's true. The coastal road is about twenty kilometers, which takes roughly three hours.
Mira: Then we'd have an hour left for lunch.
Ben: Hmm, a little tight. Unless we take the early ferry at eight.
Mira: That's better, because we'd have nine hours. I'll set my alarm for six.
Ben: Good. In that case, I'll book the bicycles online tonight.

To walk around the island

taking the early ferry

In addition
Similarly
items.why: 오래 회의했지만 결정은 안 났다는 양보/대조 관계예요.

items.q:
Thus의 뜻과 가장 가까운 것은?
The evidence was clear. Thus, the committee changed its plan.
o: Meanwhile
Instead
Therefore
Likewise
items.why: Thus는 '따라서'라는 결과/결론 표지예요.

items.q:
글쓴이가 마라톤 완주 이야기를 든 목적은?
It is never too late to start something new. For example, my neighbor ran her first marathon at sixty.
o: 마라톤 규칙을 설명하려고
이웃을 비판하려고
주장을 뒷받침하는 사례를 보여 주려고
달리기 장비를 광고하려고
items.why: For example 뒤의 사례가 첫 문장의 주장을 뒷받침해요.

items.q:
다음 글의 두 번째 문장은 첫 번째 문장과 어떤 관계인가?
Coffee is popular worldwide. In Korea alone, people drink billions of cups a year.
o: 구체적인 예·수치로 뒷받침한다
첫 문장과 정반대의 의견을 말한다
시간 순서를 바꾼다
새로운 문제를 제기한다
items.why: 두 번째 문장은 첫 번째 주장의 구체적 뒷받침이에요.

items.q: Similarly의 쓰임이 알맞은 곳은?
o: He failed the exam. Similarly, he passed it with ease.
It was cold in the room. Similarly, we turned on the fan to cool down.
I opened the window. Similarly, the room was stuffy.
Cats need regular exercise. Similarly, dogs need to be walked daily.
items.why: Similarly는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 써요.

items.q:
다음 글에서 'the former'가 가리키는 것은?
Tom and Lisa both applied for the job. The former was invited to an interview, but the latter was not.
o: Lisa
Tom
the job
the interview
items.why: the former는 앞에 언급한 둘 중 먼저 나온 것(Tom)이에요.

items.q:
다음 글의 흐름상 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
By the end of the week, the plants on the shaded window had grown much less than those in the sun. This suggests that ______.
o: light is important for healthy growth
plants prefer a cold room during the winter
water harms young leaves
shade makes plants taller
items.why: 햇빛을 받은 식물이 더 많이 자랐다는 결과로부터의 결론이에요.

items.q: Therefore를 쓰기에 가장 알맞은 문장은?
o: We watched the match. Therefore, the moon is far away.
The sky was blue. Therefore, but I stayed inside.
The ticket was sold out. Therefore, we watched the match at home.
Football is popular. Therefore, tennis is not.
items.why: 표를 못 구한 결과 집에서 보았다는 인과가 가장 자연스러워요.

items.q:
다음 단락의 주제문으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
______ Plastic bags can last hundreds of years, and they often end up in the sea, where animals mistake them for food.
o: Shopping bags are available in many colors.
Plastic bags cause serious problems for the environment.
The sea is the best place to relax.
Animals eat fewer meals in winter.
items.why: 뒤의 내용이 첫 문장을 구체적으로 뒷받침해요.

items.q: 글의 전개 방식이 '비교·대조'인 것은?
o: First, mix the flour and water in a bowl. Then bake the bread for an hour.
Because it rained, the festival was moved indoors.
The word 'tablet' comes from an old language.
Trains are quiet and steady, while buses can reach small villages.
items.why: while로 두 교통수단의 차이를 대비해요.

items.q: 글의 전개 방식이 '시간 순서'인 것은?
o: Cats are quiet and clean at home, but dogs are noisy and playful outdoors.
Cities grow because people look for jobs.
One example is the library, another is the park.
First she packed her bag; later she called a taxi; finally she left.
items.why: First, later, finally가 시간 순서를 나타내요.

items.q: Otherwise를 올바르게 쓴 문장은?
o: Leave now. Otherwise, you will arrive early and happy.
Leave now. Otherwise, you will miss the bus.
I like soup. Otherwise, I like tea too.
It is sunny. Otherwise, we went out.
items.why: otherwise는 '그렇지 않으면'이라는 조건적 결과를 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 글에서 'They'가 가리키는 것은?
The engineers showed the farmers the new pumps. They were made of steel and needed no electricity.
o: the engineers
the farmers
the pumps
the wells
items.why: 강철로 만들어졌고 전기가 필요 없는 것은 펌프예요.

items.good: Although it was raining, we played outside.
items.ko: 비가 오고 있었지만 우리는 밖에서 놀았다.
bad: Although it was raining, but we played outside.
Despite it was raining, we played outside.
Although the rain, we played outside.

cz.st: ___ it was raining, we played outside.

items.rule: Although는 접속사로 뒤에 '주어+동사'가 오고 but과 함께 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 뒤에 주어와 동사가 오는 '양보' 표현을 찾아 보세요.

items.good: In spite of the noise, she kept reading.
bad: In spite of it was noisy, she kept reading.
In spite the noise, she kept reading.
In spite of the noise, but she kept reading.

cz.st: In spite ___ the noise, she kept reading.

items.rule: In spite of는 전치사구라서 뒤에 명사(구)가 오고, 고정된 표현이에요.

items.good: The flight was delayed because of the storm.
bad: The flight was delayed because the storm.
The flight was delayed because of the storm was strong.
The flight was delayed because of that stormy.

cz.st: The flight was delayed ___ the storm.

items.rule: because of 뒤에는 명사(구)가 와요. because 뒤에는 절이 와야 해요.

items.good: You will not pass unless you study.
bad: You will not pass unless you do not study.
You will not pass unless you will study.
You will not pass if unless you study.

cz.st: You will not pass ___ you study.

items.rule: unless는 'if ... not'의 뜻이라 뒤에 다시 부정을 쓰지 않고, 미래 의미도 현재형으로 써요.

items.good: The test was so difficult that nobody finished it.
items.ko: 시험이 너무 어려워서 아무도 끝내지 못했다.
bad: The test was so difficult what nobody finished it.
The test was such difficult that nobody finished it.
The test was too difficult that nobody finished it.

cz.st: The test was ___ difficult that nobody finished it.

items.rule: so + 형용사 + that ~ (너무 ...해서 ~하다) 구문이에요. such 뒤에는 명사가 와요.

items.good: Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
items.ko: 그녀는 이겼을 뿐만 아니라 기록도 깼다.
bad: Not only she won, but she also broke the record.
Not only did she won, but she also broke the record.
Not only she did win, but she also broke the record.

cz.st: Not only ___ she win, but she also broke the record.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 동사의 순서가 바뀌어요(did + 주어 + 동사원형).

items.good: My brother likes spicy food, whereas I prefer mild dishes.
items.ko: 내 남동생은 매운 음식을 좋아하지만 나는 순한 요리를 더 좋아한다.
bad: My brother likes spicy food, whereas I prefers mild dishes.
My brother likes spicy food, whereas because I prefer mild dishes.
My brother likes spicy food, whereas prefer mild dishes I.

cz.st: My brother likes spicy food, ___ I prefer mild dishes.

items.rule: whereas는 두 절을 대조할 때 쓰는 접속사로 뒤에 '주어+동사'가 와요.

items.good: As a result of the heavy snow, the school closed.
bad: As a result the heavy snow, the school closed.
As a result of the heavy snow, so the school closed.
As a result of the heavy snow was, the school closed.

cz.st: As a result ___ the heavy snow, the school closed.

items.rule: as a result of + 명사(구)는 원인을 나타내요. 접속사 so를 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: If the ice melts, the sea level will rise.
bad: If the ice will melt, the sea level will rise.
If the ice melt, the sea level will rise.
If the ice melts, the sea level will rises.

cz.st: If the ice ___, the sea level will rise.

items.rule: if절에서는 미래의 일도 현재 시제로 쓰고, 3인칭 단수 주어에는 -s를 붙여요.

items.good: Neither the manager nor the workers were told about the change.
items.ko: 관리자도 직원들도 그 변경에 대해 듣지 못했다.
bad: Neither the manager and the workers were told about the change.
Neither the manager nor the workers was told about the change.
Neither the manager nor neither the workers were told about the change.

cz.st: Neither the manager ___ the workers were told about the change.

items.rule: neither는 nor와 짝을 이루고, 동사는 가까운 주어(the workers)에 맞춰요.

items.good: No sooner had he sat down than the phone rang.
bad: No sooner he had sat down than the phone rang.
No sooner had he sat down that the phone rang.
No sooner had he sit down than the phone rang.

cz.st: No sooner had he sat down ___ the phone rang.

items.rule: No sooner + had + 주어 + 과거분사 + than ~ 형태로 '~하자마자'를 나타내요.
